title: The mouth’s taste and the belly
odia:
ପାଟି ସୁଆଦ
ପେଟ କି ଜାଣଇ ତହିଁରେ ଭେଦ?
literal_meaning: Taste is for the mouth; does the belly know the difference?
meaning_odia: ସୁଆଦ ପାଟିର କଥା; ପେଟ ସେଥିରେ ଭେଦ ଜାଣେ କି ବୋଲି ଢଗଟି ପଚାରେ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ସୁଆଦର ପସନ୍ଦ ଓ ଖାଇ ପେଟ ପୂରାଇବାର ଦରକାରକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖାଏ। ଏହା ଖାଦ୍ୟର ପୋଷକଗୁଣ ବା ଶରୀର ବିଷୟରେ ବୈଜ୍ଞାନିକ ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ। ମୂଳ ଲେଖାରେ ତହିଁରେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ଇକାର ଚିହ୍ନଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସଜାଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The mouth values flavour, while the question imagines the belly as unconcerned with that distinction. Our editorial reading separates the pleasure of a particular taste from the simpler need to be fed. It is a rhetorical contrast, not a claim that different foods have identical effects.
usage_example: Original imagined example: During a journey, someone rejects an adequate simple meal because it is not their favourite flavour. A companion recalls the mouth-and-belly contrast to distinguish preference from the immediate need for food.
cultural_context: Two parts of one body become different voices in the argument: the mouth stands for taste, and the belly for being fed. The short first line names the preference; the question then challenges how far that preference matters.
